label: early original-phase input u/e/v/n (positions 1-2)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.5% of mass), at positions 1-3 (t=1: 64% of mass, t=2: 30%, t=3: 5%). It never fires at t=0 or in the copy phase. The input token sets how often it fires: u, e, v, n give the highest rates (lift 4-7x), then 3, c, q. Strongest examples are u or e at t=2-3 after v (e.g. b v [u], d v [u]); preceding v/n/j/e also raise the firing rate. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token. The predicate captures about 80% of activation mass, but precision is only about 0.33: these tokens at t=1-2 often stay below threshold, depending on the preceding/first token in ways not fully captured. It does not fire on delimiter or copy-phase steps, or on later original positions (t>=4).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: u, e, v, n; t=2: u, e, v, n; t=3: e, u, v, n) and the previous input (most: v, n, j, q, e, 3; least: b, d, i, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, L=3 & t=4, t=1.
